summary: The video reviews seven websites focused on narrow home services, with local SEO pages and subcontractors used to serve customers across multiple cities. An unnamed operator describes running a junk removal business remotely by booking jobs online and dispatching them to subcontractors. The host also lists additional home service niches that could use a similar approach. The examples illustrate a way to acquire and coordinate work, but most provide no verified operating figures or evidence that the proposed niches will be profitable.

tactics.name: Target one service and one keyword
steps: Choose a narrow home service with a clear search phrase.
Build a website focused on that service rather than presenting a broad list of unrelated services.
Expand into nearby locations after establishing the initial service focus.

quote.text: They just focus on a single service and one single keyword.
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

tactics.name: Build local pages for a focused service
steps: Create pages for the chosen service in each target city.
Use the service and city together in the page targeting.
Expand coverage only where service delivery can be arranged.

quote.text: They built out a whole website with pages dedicated to each city that they want to rank for.
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

tactics.name: Dispatch online bookings to subcontractors
steps: Accept job details through a website.
Send each booked job to a local subcontractor.
Have the subcontractor perform the physical work while the operator coordinates remotely.

quote.text: So, I book jobs online on our website and send the jobs out to the subcontractors, and they go do the labor, pick up the junk for me, and I just manage it all remotely from the computer.
quote.speaker: Unnamed junk removal operator

tactics.name: Make simple bookings self-serve
steps: Let customers enter a zip code and choose the item to be removed.
Show a guaranteed price for the described job.
Allow customers to select a day, book, and pay online.
Send the resulting job to a subcontractor.

quote.text: You can choose the day and actually book and pay online.
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

tactics.name: Use a focused service to expand into more locations
steps: Start with a specific service in one location.
Build pages for other locations after identifying a service and keyword that can rank.
Use subcontractors or local providers where the company expands.

lessons.lesson: A narrow service and search phrase can make a small operator look like a specialist in a local market.

quote.text: I found a lot of success in my business going after very specific keywords and services in very specific locations.
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

lessons.lesson: Local service pages can extend a focused offer into additional cities, but the video does not show that rankings automatically produce profitable work.

quote.text: Some of them have even expanded ranking for this single service in a bunch of cities.
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

lessons.lesson: Subcontractors can let an operator coordinate work remotely while other people perform the physical service.
